Text.Text: Alpha Rhythm. You found the true beat and you're keeping it, on your own now. Preserve doesn't need me tapping it out for you anymore. Go make some music.

Listen. Hear that? Off, just slightly, coming from past the tree line. That's the preserve, out of time with itself. You're out of time too, your own beast isn't following your beat yet. Come back when it is.

There it is again, that wrong beat, six of them making it. Adepts, driving beasts to a rhythm that isn't theirs, forcing a lead where none should be. Go into the Tarn Jungle Preserve on Dathomir. Put the six down. Bring me back the Alpha Rhythm Tarn Hunt Tally; it's got the true count scratched into it somewhere under all that noise.
Take the key. South gate, past the drum-bark trees; you'll hear why we call them that once you're close. Go find the true count and bring it home.

A forced lead sets a rhythm the whole line has to follow whether it wants to or not. Adepts goad a beast into that position instead of letting one earn it. Sounds close to a real pack rhythm if you don't know better. It isn't. It's just noise wearing a beat's shape.
A true lead doesn't force tempo. It offers one, and the pack chooses to follow because the choice keeps everyone alive together. That's rhythm. Command without choice is just noise with good timing.

Every true count this preserve ever kept got scratched onto that tally, generation over generation. Adepts use it to fake a rhythm they never earned. Bring it back and the true count's mine to read again, not theirs to counterfeit.
Six adepts still keeping that wrong beat. Tally's still with them.
You're moving different. Steadier. Let me see what you brought back.
There's the true count, home again. Preserve's already sitting a little straighter for it. More noise further in, if you want to keep quieting it.

Five specialists past the adepts, and they've got a scent vial dosing the pens to force a tempo the beasts can't refuse. That's not leading a pack. That's playing a drum nobody agreed to march to. Go put the five down. Bring me the Alpha Rhythm Beast-Pen Scent Vial.
Same gate, deeper in. Listen for the drum-bark trees to go quiet; that's how you'll know you're close to the pens.

Dosed to force a tempo through scent alone, no choosing involved anywhere in it. Bring that vial back and I've got the forced beat isolated, proof of exactly how they've been playing this preserve like an instrument that never agreed to be played.

Earning a beat takes patience. Forcing one takes a vial and no conscience. They chose the vial because it's faster, and because a pack that's forced doesn't ask questions about who's leading it. Efficient. Also completely dishonest.

No. A pack under a forced tempo isn't moving together, it's just moving at the same time, which sounds the same for about a beat and a half before it falls apart. True rhythm holds because every player in it is choosing the same beat freely. Force it, and the first missed step brings the whole line down.
Five specialists still forcing that beat. Bring the vial back.
You've got the rhythm of it now, I think. Let's hear what you brought.
Forced beat, isolated and dead. That's proof this preserve can use. You're keeping better time every visit.

Warden holds the deep pens, and he's the one who taught the specialists to force a beat in the first place. His rhythm's fast, and it's alone, and a single follower just gets swept along by it instead of matching it. Bring two more players of your own; a pack answers a rhythm better than one dancer ever could. Put him down. Bring me the Alpha Rhythm Clawed Alpha Totem he's carrying.
Same gate. Go together, and listen to each other as much as you listen to him. A pack that isn't syncing with itself won't sync against him either.

Fast, relentless, alone. He set that tempo himself once, honestly, before the crew got their hands on him and taught him to force it onto anyone standing near. Half the man I remember is still in that beat somewhere. The other half is exactly why you need company.

Alpha totem marks the true lead of a pack line, the one every follower chose freely. He's carrying it clawed apart because he stopped being a true lead the day he started forcing his beat instead of earning it. Bring it back whole and the true lead is honored again.

One dancer against a fast solo rhythm just gets swept along, always a half-step behind, always reacting instead of matching. Three, moving together, and one of you can always be on his beat while the others answer from the gaps. That's not extra safety. That's the only way to actually keep time with something that fast.
Warden's beat is still fast, still alone. Gather your pack and answer it.
Your whole pack still moving. Good rhythm holds. Let me see the totem.
Whole. The true lead's honored again, first time in longer than this preserve's kept count. Rest your pack. The ones who taught him that beat are next, and they know it's coming.

Four keepers left, the ones who wrote the forced tempo into doctrine and taught it as if it were the real rhythm all along. Bring your pack back in; four beats at once, out of sync with each other on purpose, is worse than one fast soloist. Put them down. Bring me the Alpha Rhythm Preserve Keeper's Token they hold between them.
Same gate, deepest part of the preserve. Four beats, deliberately out of sync with each other to confuse anyone listening. Keep your pack listening to each other first, them second.

Force instead of earn, drum instead of offer, and they wrote it all down and taught it like scripture to anyone who'd listen. A pack built on that never actually moves together. It just moves at the same time, right up until it doesn't, and then it's four soloists standing where a pack used to be.

That token's the true count of who's allowed to call tempo for this whole preserve. They minted false copies to cover for each other. One real token in my hands, and every false beat they've called since gets silenced with it.

Because one player can only answer one beat at a time, and a rhythm this deliberately broken throws more beats at you than one player can track. A pack of your own splits the listening. Somebody's always got the next beat covered, even when it's coming from four directions at once.
Four keepers, still playing their broken time signature. Bring the token back.
Whole pack, still together. Let's hear what you brought.
Whole. Their false beat's silenced for good. One rhythm left down there, and it's the one every other broken beat in this preserve got copied from. Your pack's ready for that one, I think.

Last rhythm. The master's beat is seductive, and that's the danger of it, it sounds almost like a true lead's tempo, close enough that a whole pack will follow it without noticing the wrongness until it's too late. He built that out of the same rhythm I've spent my life teaching honestly. Bring your whole pack. One player following that beat alone gets pulled all the way in before they realize which rhythm they're actually keeping. There's no token this time. His rhythm breaking, for good, is the whole proof.
Then go, all together, same gate as always. Listen to each other first. His beat wants you listening only to him.

Because it's not a lie built from nothing. It's the true rhythm, the one I've spent my life teaching, bent just enough that it still sounds honest while it forces everyone near it to follow. You've been learning to offer a beat and let a pack choose it freely. He learned the same beat and decided choosing was optional. That's the whole difference, and it's the whole danger.

Because a soloist following a seductive rhythm alone has nothing to check it against, no second beat reminding them what true tempo actually feels like. A whole pack, playing their own honest rhythm together, gives each other something to hold onto when his beat tries to pull everyone into his time instead. That's not extra caution. That's the only defense a rhythm like his actually has an answer to.

Goes back to true tempo, offered and chosen, the way a pack's supposed to move. I'll be listening for it every day after this, and the day it sounds honest again all the way through, I'll know you finished the job right.
His beat's still playing, still seductive. Bring your whole pack when you go.
Quiet. Whole preserve's gone quiet, no beat at all, first time in longer than I've been listening. Tell me it's him.

Then the rhythm's true again, all the way through. That's Alpha Rhythm, finished: a beat offered, not forced, and a pack that chooses to follow because the choice keeps everyone alive together. You learned to hear it. Now go keep it. Your beast already knows the tempo. Trust it.
Back to the beat.
I'll quiet the six and bring the tally.
What do you mean, a wrong beat?
How does a lead beast set tempo for a pack?
What's this tally to your rhythm?
Let me listen a while longer.
Here's the Alpha Rhythm Tarn Hunt Tally.
Back to the beat.
I'll quiet the five and bring the vial.
What's the vial doing to the tempo?
Why force a beat instead of earning one?
Can a pack even move honestly under a forced tempo?
Give me a little more time.
Here's the Alpha Rhythm Beast-Pen Scent Vial.
Back to the beat.
I'll bring two more players and answer his beat together.
What's his rhythm like, exactly?
What does the alpha totem mean in your rhythm-language?
Why does one player fail against his tempo?
My pack isn't gathered yet.
Here's the Alpha Rhythm Clawed Alpha Totem, whole.
Back to the beat.
We'll answer all four beats together.
What did they turn into doctrine?
What does the keeper's token mean to your rhythm?
Why does breaking a rhythm need more than one player?
My pack needs rest first.
Here's the Alpha Rhythm Preserve Keeper's Token, whole.
Back to the beat.
Our whole pack, answering his beat together.
What makes his rhythm so seductive?
Why can't even a skilled soloist break it alone?
What happens to the preserve's rhythm, once he's gone?
Not until every player's ready.
It's done. His beat broke.
